Class OpenSearchClient

java.lang.Object
org.mavendb.loader.OpenSearchClient
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
final class OpenSearchClient extends Object implements AutoCloseable
Minimal OpenSearch REST client for the bulk load, on the JDK HttpClient: no client library needed.

Load cycle of one index:

  1. recreateIndex(String, String): drop the index and create it from db/opensearch/create.json, tuned for loading: no replicas, refresh disabled, asynchronous translog
  2. bulk(String, byte[], int, long): one _bulk request per batch, from several writers
  3. finishLoad(String): restore search settings and refresh, so all documents become searchable

Thread safe: HttpClient is shared by all writers.

  • Method Details

    • toBulkData

      static byte[] toBulkData(List<org.bson.Document> documents)
      Encode documents as a _bulk request body (NDJSON): an index action with the document id, then the source.

      The _id field becomes the OpenSearch document id: it is metadata and must not be in the source. Thread safe: called on the conversion threads, so the writer only sends bytes.

      Parameters:
      documents - Documents with an _id field; the field is removed from each document
      Returns:
      Request body, UTF-8

    • splitBulk

      static List<int[]> splitBulk(byte[] data, int maxBytes)
      Split a bulk body into requests of at most maxBytes, at document boundaries (every second line).

      A batch has a fixed number of documents, but documents vary from 1 KB to over 1 MB (a long Export-Package), so a batch of large documents can pass http.max_content_length and fail with HTTP 413. A single document larger than maxBytes is sent alone. Splitting on the raw '\n' byte is safe: JSON escapes newlines in strings, and no UTF-8 multi-byte sequence contains that byte.

      Parameters:
      data - Bulk body, see toBulkData(List)
      maxBytes - Request size limit
      Returns:
      Ranges [start, end) covering all of data, in order
